elements.element: Customer may terminate the Agreement or an Order Form for convenience.
elements.evidence: Inserted: "Licensee may terminate this Agreement for convenience upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to Licensor". The element is disjunctive and this Software License and Maintenance Agreement has no Order Form structure, so the Agreement-level right suffices.

elements.element: Customer's convenience termination requires no more than 30 days' written notice.
elements.evidence: "upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to Licensor" — exactly 30 days, written, and no additional conditions or approvals attached.

elements.element: Vendor refunds prepaid fees pro rata after Customer's convenience termination.
elements.evidence: "Licensor shall refund pro rata any prepaid fees for the period after the effective date of termination" — express pro-rata basis, not merely a post-termination-period refund.

elements.element: Vendor has no right to terminate for convenience during a committed term.
elements.evidence: "Licensor shall have no right to terminate this Agreement for convenience during the Initial Period or any renewal or extension term." Retained Article IV Licensor rights are breach-based immediate termination and an option to renew, which do not contradict this.

elements.element: Customer may terminate for convenience on 60 to 90 days' notice.
elements.evidence: The inserted right runs on thirty (30) days' notice, which is outside the 60–90 day fallback band (more Customer-favourable, but literally not the fallback term).

elements.element: Any early-termination fee is capped at three months of fees.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: neither the retained Article IV nor the insertion imposes any early-termination fee or contingent payment on Licensee's convenience exit, so no cap is required.

elements.element: Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term.
elements.evidence: Licensor is given no convenience right at all during the Initial Period or any renewal/extension term, which is at least as restrictive as an end-of-term-only right; renewal is an option, not a convenience termination.

elements.element: Vendor must give at least 90 days' notice of convenience termination.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: Licensor has no convenience termination right under the rendered language, so no notice period is needed.

elements.element: Customer may terminate the Agreement or an Order Form for convenience.
elements.evidence: Not a fallback element; noted only for completeness — the operative insertion grants Licensee an Agreement-level convenience right.

reasons: Preferred level is complete: all four preferred elements appear in operative language (30 days' written notice, express pro-rata refund of prepaid fees, and an express bar on Licensor convenience termination during the Initial Period and any renewal/extension term).
Fallback is incomplete only on the notice band (30 days rather than 60–90 days); this is immaterial because the preferred checklist is fully met.

Minimal: the insertion adds two sentences and deletes nothing from Article IV. The drafter correctly omitted the model-language surplus "in whole or in part" (no Order Form or partial-termination structure exists) and added no survival tail, procedure, or extra remedies.

Intent preserved: the retained Article IV term, renewal option, breach-based immediate termination, and Licensor's right to trade-based payments all survive without contradiction; "Subject to termination pursuant to this Agreement" in Article IV I now accommodates the new right, and "Initial Period" is a defined term so no dangling reference is created.
No repairs required. If the counterparty pushes back, the comment's offer of 60 days plus a three-month fee cap would need to be rendered in operative text to count.
